prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” personal injury lawyer for every car wreck — the right lawyer depends on your case (how serious the injuries are, whether fault is disputed, whether you want to go to trial), your location, and your preferences. I can help you find strong candidates, but here are practical steps and tips so you can get the best lawyer for your situation.

How to choose the right car-wreck lawyer
- Look for experience with car-crash cases and similar injuries (whiplash, fractures, TBI, wrongful death). Trial experience is important if the insurer won’t settle.  
- Proven results: sizable verdicts/settlements in comparable cases. Ask for examples (names may be confidential, but firms can describe results).  
- Reputation and reviews: check client reviews and peer ratings (Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, Avvo, Google).  
- Communication and availability: you want a lawyer who returns calls and explains options.  
- Fee structure: most personal injury lawyers work on contingency (no upfront fee; they take a percentage of recovery). Ask the exact percentage and who pays costs if you don’t recover.  
- Local knowledge: a Houston lawyer who knows local courts, judges, medical providers and opposing insurers is an advantage.  
- Clean disciplinary record: verify with the State Bar of Texas.

What to ask at a free consultation
- Have you handled many car-wreck cases like mine? What were the results?  
- Do you take cases to trial? How often have you gone to trial?  
- Who exactly will handle my case (attorney vs. paralegal)?  
- What is your contingency fee? What additional costs might I owe?  
- How will you communicate updates and how often?  
- What is your estimate of the case value and timeline?

Documents and information to bring to a consultation
- Police report, photos of the crash and damage, contact info for the other driver and witnesses.  
- Medical records and bills, emergency room notes, doctors’ names and contact info.  
- Insurance information (your policy and the other driver’s).  
- Pay stubs if you have lost income.

Practical items to know
- Statute of limitations in Texas for most car-accident injury claims is 2 years from the date of the crash — don’t wait.  
- Typical contingency fees are often about 33% for settlements and can be higher (e.g., 40%) if the case is filed and goes to trial — always confirm in writing.  
- If you have serious injuries, consider a lawyer sooner rather than later so evidence and witness statements aren’t lost.

Resources to find and vet Houston lawyers
- State Bar of Texas (disciplinary records)  
- Super Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo (ratings and reviews)  
- Google/Yelp reviews and local consumer-protection sites  
- Recommendations from friends, family, or medical providers

If you want, I can:
- Recommend several well-reviewed Houston personal injury attorneys and law firms near you (I’ll need your ZIP code or neighborhood), or  
- Draft a short list of questions to send by email to firms, or  
- Help you evaluate a specific lawyer you’re already considering.

Tell me your ZIP code or the rough location in Houston and a few details about the crash (severity of injuries, whether fault is disputed), and I’ll pull together 3–5 attorneys/firms to consider.
